status: declared before any model score; owner (20 Nov): 'Let's do 3' (runoff / hydrology, item 3 of the fixable-parts list)
question: Does the model's monthly runoff (polity/seasons.py: snow bucket, 100 mm soil bucket, Hargreaves PET) have the right seasonal shape — the input to the river flood and low-water indices — and does another bucket size or PET method match better?
target: GRUN v1 (Ghiggi et al. 2019, ESSD 11:1655; figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.9228176, CC BY 4.0), observation-based monthly runoff at 0.5 deg, ensemble mean; averaged to a 1970-2000 monthly climatology (the WorldClim period); data/cache/grun, not redistributed
model: polity.seasons.fields on WorldClim 2.1 monthly tavg/tmax/tmin/prec at 5 arc-min over the Earth run window (0-56 N, 12 W - 125 E), runoff averaged to 0.5 deg
variants: soil bucket SOIL_MM in {25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300} x PET in {hargreaves, droogers_allen}: 12 variants; current = 100 mm, hargreaves
domain: 0.5-deg cells with >= 50 % land in both grids; shape scored on 2.5-deg blocks (5 x 5 cells, >= 13 valid) with GRUN annual runoff >= 20 mm
split: 10-degree checkerboard of block centres: dev even, blind odd

scores.primary_shape: median over blocks of the Pearson correlation between model and GRUN 12-month runoff, each divided by its own annual mean
scores.flood_months: F1 of block-months with relative flow > 1.5 (the map's flood start), model vs GRUN
scores.annual: Spearman of annual runoff over 0.5-deg cells (reported; the map uses relative flows only)

choice: variant with the highest dev primary_shape

blind_gates.V: current blind primary_shape >= 0.6 -> seasonal pattern supported
blind_gates.adopt: G1 and G2: the river flow and flood indices use the chosen bucket/PET (mud keeps its own adopted setting, tested separately at stations); part of the bundled rebuild. Otherwise current stays and V is reported.
